ruling.recommended_action: Refund $6.90 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) for the unexempted off-route mileage on the 17:37–17:53 segment; no account flag (RD-6 not met).
ruling.reasoning:
The 17:37–17:53 off-route segment is measured: 7.60 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.70 km, +4.89 km, up to 1268 m off the optimal route, plus a 4 min 10 s stationary stop at a point 4918 m from pickup and 5158 m from drop-off [F4][F2]. That opens RD-1: no percentage or kilometre threshold is set, and any deviation not excused by RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 is an unexempted detour. No traffic excuse is available — the trace records no qualifying incident [F15] and the only bands on the corridor are band 4, far above the band 1–2 congestion bands (RD-4(b) does not exempt alone) [F13][F14][RD-4].

The rider did ask for a stop before the segment: at 17:33 she wrote "Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way? Just need 2 minutes." and the driver replied "Sure" at 17:34, ahead of the 17:37:50 segment start [F9][F10][F4]. But the words name no road, no area and no outlet — they ask for a stop, not a route [F9]. RD-3(a) exempts a rider-named stop only where the rider named a specific place and the car stopped there; "a 7-Eleven on the way" names a kind, not a place, and the driver's own post-trip statement says he chose the outlet ("I went to the one I know") [F12][RD-3]. RD-3(b) is directly on point: a stop the rider asked for without naming a place, where the driver selected the location and created an off-route segment, does not exempt that segment's extra_km [RD-3]. RD-5 is likewise unavailable: what was agreed was a short stop (a "scope_other" kind of agreement), and a driver's statement of what the rider wanted is a claim, not rider consent [F12][RD-5]. The open question therefore resolves as counts on the ground the rider advocate named (scope_other); the driver's rider_named_stop reading fails on the words of F9 read with F12.

Amount: the trip is RydeTAXI, so excess metered mileage is chargeable [F5][F6][F8][RD-2]. Rate = fare.distance_fare ÷ distance_km = $29.53 ÷ 20.94 km = $1.4102/km [F8]. Unexempted extra_km on F4 = 4.89 km. 4.89 km × $1.4102/km = $6.8959 → $6.90 [F4][F5][RD-2]. The waiting charge is not refunded: RydeTAXI waiting is metered and chargeable, and both advocates now concede it [F6][RD-3(c)].

No account flag: RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1, and the driver profile records route: 0, no-show: 0 with the single upheld dispute being of another kind, so the predicate is absent [F18][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's 17:33 message asks only for a stop ('Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way? Just need 2 minutes.', accepted 'Sure' at 17:34), naming no road, area or outlet, and the driver's own statement says he chose the outlet ('I went to the one I know') [F9][F10][F12]. RD-3(a) does not exempt a stop whose place the rider did not name; RD-3(b) leaves the segment's extra_km counted when the driver's undisclosed chosen location creates the off-route segment; RD-5 consent here covers a short stop, not this 7.60 km loop reaching 1268 m off the optimal route [F4][RD-3][RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: Timing alone is not scope: the 17:33 message precedes the 17:37 segment, but it names no route or road, and RD-5 consent covers only what the words agree to — a stop, not the route driven to the driver's chosen outlet [F9][F10][F4][F12][RD-5].

RD-3(a) requires the rider to have named a specific place; 'a 7-Eleven on the way' names a kind, and the record shows an off-route segment rather than a stop on the optimal corridor, so the segment is not exempt under RD-3(a) [F9][F4][F2][RD-3].

The driver's statement that he chose the outlet is a driver claim, not rider consent, and an undisclosed driver-chosen stop point that creates an off-route segment does not exempt that segment's extra_km [F12][F4][F9][RD-3][RD-5].
The single stationary period is the stop itself; RD-3(a) does not exempt the driving that produced the off-route segment merely because the stop is the only stationary period [F2][F4][RD-3].

Leaving the choice of outlet to the driver does not extend the rider's 'on the way' instruction to a 7.60 km drive reaching 1268 m off the optimal route; the agreed scope was a short stop, so the segment counts [F9][F4][F12][RD-1][RD-3][RD-5].
RD-6's predicate is route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1; the driver profile records route: 0 and no-show: 0, so no flag attaches [F18][RD-6].
Same record defeats the flag request: the one upheld dispute is not a route dispute within 90 days, so RD-6 is not triggered [F18][RD-6].
